subject.title: Vertex beta INVALID_ARGUMENT can wedge long sessions without actionable recovery

question: For LiteLLM/Vertex beta generic 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT after long context buildup, should OpenClaw classify it as recoverable session/provider state, context overflow, model fallback, or only actionable user guidance until live evidence proves a safer recovery?
rationale: The source gap is real, but generic INVALID_ARGUMENT can mean several provider-side problems; choosing compaction/fallback/reset behavior affects provider routing and session state semantics.

options.title: Require live proof, then add narrow provider-owned recovery

options.title: Only improve user guidance now
options.body: Surface a clearer provider-rejected-request message without automatic compaction, fallback, or reset until the failure mode is proven live.

options.body: Route this shape through context overflow recovery, accepting the risk that unrelated INVALID_ARGUMENT failures may be misclassified.
